Recent indicators suggest the economy is expanding at a solid pace, but the Committee’s hold at 5.25–5.50% and ongoing balance‑sheet runoff align with the Taylor‑rule perspective that policy should remain restrictive while inflation exceeds target (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler). With unemployment low and job gains still strong, New Keynesian Phillips Curve logic implies persistent cost pressures until slack increases, justifying the Fed’s insistence on “greater confidence” before cutting and its inflation‑forecast‑targeting emphasis (Svensson and Woodford). The pledge to return inflation to 2% also addresses time‑inconsistency/inflation‑bias concerns from classic monetary theory, while continued QT works through term premia in the transmission mechanism. Overall, growth and disinflation progress are modestly positive, but the hawkish hold and vigilance to right‑tail inflation risks temper the tone.
